name: Vienna Game
blurb: White plays 2.Nc3 and then often f4, a King's Gambit with the knight already out. Aggressive but more solid than the King's Gambit itself.

lines.name: Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defense
Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defense

ideas.e4: Takes a central square and opens lines for the queen and bishop.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3: Develops the knight and covers d5, keeping the f-pawn free to advance.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4: The Vienna Gambit. The f-pawn attacks e5, as in the King's Gambit, but with the knight already developed.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5: Takes the pawn, and the new pawn on e5 attacks the f6 knight.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5 Nxe4 Nf3: Develops and protects the e5 pawn, so Black's knight on e4 has no easy target.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5 d4 exf6: Black's d-pawn attacks the c3 knight, so White grabs the f6 knight first.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 exf4 e5: Kicks the knight from f6 before winning back the f4 pawn.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 f4: The same gambit against ...Nc6: the f-pawn hits e5 and the f-file can open for the rook.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 f4 exf4 Nf3: Develops and stops ...Qh4+, which would be check now that the f-pawn is gone.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4: Attacks the g5 pawn, which is the one holding Black's extra pawn on f4.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Bc5 Nf3: Develops and attacks e5. With Black's bishop aiming at f2, quiet development is safer than an early f4.
ideas.e4 e5 Nc3 Bb4 Nf3: Develops with an attack on e5, which nothing defends after Black's bishop move.
